text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said in a radio interview on Wednesday that he believed Federal Reserve chief Alan Greenspan was "not completely unjustified" with his comments on the "irrational exuberance" of markets.

But, according to an editorial version of the interview released in advance of the broadcast, Welteke went on to say that the strong rise in German share prices and low German interest rates were a sign of trust in the German economy.
Greenspan on Wednesday denied that his "irrational exuberance" reference, first made in December, had been aimed at talking the U.S. stock market down.
In the interview, Welteke also repeated that he saw no reason for an interest rate cut to help the German economy.
He added that reducing high joblessness was the major task of the German economy at the moment, but that the Bundesbank had done all it could to create good conditions for growth.

He added that the general uncertainty in the economy soured the atmosphere for the introduction of the European single currency, but said Germans need not worry that their purchasing power would be eroded by the introduction of the euro.
